name: José Antonio Primo de Rivera
description: Spanish Falange founder assessed from his own national-syndicalist programme, rather than the later institutions established under Franco.

religion.reason: Catholic identification and Catholic orientation are recorded in his life and own programme.

sources.title: José Antonio Primo de Rivera — biography and positions
Norma programática de FE de las JONS

axes.brief: The programme abolishes party representation in favour of a totalitarian national state.
axes.counterEvidence: Municipal and syndical participation is corporative, not competitive suffrage.

axes.brief: Individual liberty is subordinated to national unity and rigorous discipline.
axes.counterEvidence: Declared human dignity qualifies arbitrary private harm but does not create a general right to political dissent.

axes.brief: Shared Spanish destiny and Catholic national education reject separatism and competing collective loyalties.
axes.counterEvidence: His programme is spiritual-cultural, not a comprehensive biological race theory.

qualifications.15: The statement specifically includes several distinct ways of life within national identity; it does not ask whether a common national identity should exist.

axes.brief: National unity and protected labour favour managed admission and cultural integration.
axes.counterEvidence: No specific modern asylum, quota or family-sponsorship schedule is documented.

qualifications.5: The statement permits permanent refugee settlement regardless of skills or cultural compatibility. The answer concerns this unconditional clause, separately from selected humanitarian admissions.

axes.brief: Imperial ambition, strong armed forces and pre-military education give force a prominent political role.
axes.counterEvidence: A proposed revolution is not proof of every foreign operation; describing his programme as peaceful would contradict it.

axes.brief: Independence and international Spanish predominance limit external political control.
axes.counterEvidence: Cooperation with Hispanic America is intended, with Spain claiming a leading position.

axes.brief: Private initiative and family property coexist with explicit nationalisation of banking and major public services.
axes.counterEvidence: Opposition to capitalism is not abolition of all private property; the programme expressly protects compatible initiative.

axes.brief: Protected agricultural prices, tariffs and national economic integrity favour economic protection.
axes.counterEvidence: Maritime commerce and Hispanic economic cooperation prevent equating protection with ending foreign exchange.

axes.brief: Vertical syndicates, directed cultivation, national agricultural credit and price guarantees coordinate production.
axes.counterEvidence: Private initiative continues when compatible with collective interests; this is not identical to Marxist state ownership.

axes.brief: National wealth should reduce mass poverty, provide unemployment support and redistribute cultivable land.
axes.counterEvidence: Family property and work obligations constrain universal unconditional redistribution; illegitimate holdings could be expropriated without compensation.

axes.brief: Catholic tradition is incorporated into national reconstruction and education.
axes.counterEvidence: The programme rejects Church interference that undermines state dignity or national integrity; no unrestricted clergy veto follows.

axes.brief: Family-centred Catholic and martial national life favours inherited moral institutions.
axes.counterEvidence: The movement sought revolutionary political and economic change; that does not establish sexual liberalisation.

axes.brief: Hydraulic projects and improved agricultural teaching support practical innovation alongside moral and ecological constraints.
axes.counterEvidence: Compulsory reforestation and restoration are explicit; modern genetics and implants are speculative analogies.

qualifications.13: Controlled embryo-enhancement trials are still a reproductive intervention. Catholic moral commitments make rejection more likely even where practical industrial modernisation is supported.

axes.brief: Separatism is rejected and national direction dominates education, production and security.
axes.counterEvidence: Municipal participation and restored communal patrimonies give bounded local functions, not sovereign federalism.

axes.brief: National education and disciplined formation are intended to construct future character.
axes.counterEvidence: Spiritual nationalism and traditional sex roles do not establish a genetic explanation for every trait.
